story_review.one_viewing_summary: Planned chain: the server's station empties and the phone rings, no job ad goes up, and an AI host panel named Haniya lights. A guest scans, taps and pays, and the paid mark triggers the ticket and the wok. The owner's savings figure is stamped as his own count. Tips go to the jar under a FOX 26 attribution. The federal rule allows a cook pool, but the restaurant's box stays blank. A customer hesitates at the code, and the close tags the jar owner says and no record shown.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question (who takes the order) is answered by the panel and the paid-then-cooked chain. The closing tags keep the tip claim on the owner's word, which matches the source limit.
story_review.weakest_transition: s9 quote-card to s10 panel-order (53.81 s). The cut moves from a table-top quote to a medium room in which the answer action is planned at small scale.

strongest_frame: s4 paid-line into ticket-print into wok-flare (23.9 to 27.1 s). In OrderPassFilm.tsx orderState carries the paid token along a contact path into the printer slot. The lamp change, ticket rise and wok flare are all pure functions of the board clock, so 'nothing is cooked until the order is paid for' is built as one causal chain on the same objects.
weakest_frame: s10 panel-order (53.81 to 56.72 s). The closing clause 'software now takes the order' is carried by a small order card and slip arc on the host panel in a medium room view, with no guest interaction. As constructed, the action covers a small share of the frame. Its legibility is a phone-scope question.
